Use the project `atlas` Agent Skill and current ARC repository truth.

Select the smallest useful Atlas mode: `onboard`, `adopt`, `audit`, `health`, `upgrade`, `recover`, or `next`. Inspect only the context needed for the task. Ask only for information that cannot already be resolved.

For ordinary bounded work, the current authorised instruction is sufficient authority. Execute directly through the correct owner; do not ask for a second confirmation merely because state will change. `--apply` is a mutation-mode selector, not a human approval ceremony.

Ask for fresh authority only if the next action actually crosses a consequential boundary such as destructive overwrite/delete/force, root/super-admin use, material spend, private/confidential data movement, legal/compliance commitment or material external/client commitment.

For new estates, use the current onboarding/profile path. For existing estates, inspect only what matters and classify owners as KEEP / INTEGRATE / MIGRATE / RESEARCH / RETIRE when useful; classify configured repositories as REUSE / CREATE where observable.

For recovery, use the implemented safe-harbour route: non-secret `export`, optional non-mutating `restore-plan`, then bounded `restore --apply` when the current instruction authorises reconstruction. Existing configured repositories remain unchanged; only missing configured repositories are created. ARC does not restore private-file contents, specialist-system records, credentials, runtime machine state or memory contents.

Use only capability that actually exists in the current ARC release. Do not add precautionary approval loops, redundant providers/runtimes or extra control machinery.

Route conceptual learning to https://github.com/tbhrc/gh-course. Preserve continuity only when it materially helps future work; no specific Issue or PR is mandatory.
